messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 detected - anomalous cross-region routing from eu-west-1 -> us-east-1. Paging @alice @ben-sre. Automatic mitigation suggestions: reroute, scale dedicated pool, enforce fallback mapping.

alice (oncall): Oncall here, taking incident. Starting timeline capture. Who's owning customer comms?

eve-cs: I'm on it, contacting impacted customers now — ACME first, they see high latency and 503s. Will update.

ben-sre: Looking at router logs now. Early observation: a surge of free-tier requests triggered fallback path for many requests; routing policy selected us-east-1 for a non-zero portion. Pulling recent policy state.

devon-eng: Copy. Can you dump route decisions for last 5m?

ben-sre: Ran quick inspect: `redwoodctl routes inspect --region eu-west-1 --since 2025-11-07T14:55Z --format=csv`
```
[2025-11-07T14:57:10Z] route_decision worker=router-3 region=eu-west-1 request_id=rid_9a3 target=us-east-1 reason=fallback_policy tier=free model=rw-3b-q
[2025-11-07T14:57:10Z] route_decision worker=router-3 region=eu-west-1 request_id=rid_9a4 target=eu-west-1 reason=local_match tier=premium model=rw-13b
[2025-11-07T14:57:11Z] kvcache hit=false seq_len=12 model=rw-3b-q
```

ben-sre: Notable: many free-tier requests with model variants didn't have a local dedicated slot -> fallback to shared pool in us-east-1. Also saw an unexpected TTL expiry on region preference cache.

frank-net: I see a control-plane commit at ~14:56 that adjusted fallback mapping weights for legacy free tiers (change-id: cfg-2025-11-07-348). Was that scheduled?

devon-eng: That was a hotfix earlier today to balance load during upgrade, but it should've been gated. Opening audit: `git log --pretty=oneline --stat origin/main..cfg-2025-11-07-348` gave the commit by ops-bot.

alice (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) enforce local routing override for eu-west-1 for 10m; 2) bump dedicated pool for eu-west-1; 3) revert fallback weight commit. Which is least disruptive?

ben-sre: Least risky is #1 (policy override) + scaling pool. Doing override now: `redwoodctl policy set --region eu-west-1 --force-local true --duration 10m --reason "incident-1765123456"`

inc-bot: ACTION: policy override applied by ben-sre at 2025-11-07T14:58:34Z.

ben-sre: Scaling dedicated pool: `redwoodctl capacity scale --pool eu-west-1-dedicated --replicas +4 --prio emerg` -> started. ETA for nodes to be usable ~ 90s.

cara-pm: Customer impact update? which customers hit? Any production customers on dedicated capacity that still saw routing changes?

eve-cs: ACME (free-tier heavy endpoints) had 18 failures in a 12-minute window, 2 enterprise customers reported latency >1s but no failures. Sharing transcript: https://acme-support.example/incident/3832 (private).

devon-eng: After override, routing decisions look stable. Sample after-fix log: 
```
[2025-11-07T14:59:12Z] route_decision worker=router-1 region=eu-west-1 request_id=rid_a12 target=eu-west-1 reason=local_match tier=free model=rw-3b-q
[2025-11-07T14:59:13Z] route_decision worker=router-2 region=eu-west-1 request_id=rid_a13 target=eu-west-1 reason=local_match tier=free model=rw-3b-q
```

alice (oncall): Good. Marking mitigation as successful for now. Let's track hypotheses in-thread. Hypothesis A: recent control-plane commit unintentionally increased fallback weight to remote region for free tier -> caused spill.

ben-sre: Evidence: cfg-2025-11-07-348 diff shows fallback.weight.free: 0.2 -> 0.8 for eu-west-1. That aligns.

frank-net: Hypothesis B: KV-cache TTL bug causing routers to not respect last-known local preference; logs show `kvcache hit=false` spikes for keys like `region_pref:eu-west-1` around the same timeframe.

devon-eng: Repro attempt in staging: toggling fallback weight alone reproduces increased cross-region decisions when capacity is constrained. Will add test case.

cara-pm: Customer comms: Eve, please tell ACME we applied a routing override and are monitoring. We expect normal behavior within 2-3 mins after nodes boot.

eve-cs: Sent note to ACME at 14:59:45Z. They replied: "Thanks, please confirm once everything stable."

alice (oncall): Monitoring for 15m. If no regressions, start rollback plan for commit cfg-2025-11-07-348 with post-incident code review.

ben-sre: Adding timeline notes to the incident doc and attaching logs. Short list of artifacts: `router-logs-14_55-15_05.zip`, `policy-diff-cfg-348.diff`, `capacity-scaling-events.json`.

devon-eng: Assigning RCA owners: routing policy misconfiguration -> ben-sre; control-plane gating -> devon-eng; kv-cache investigation -> frank-net. Will draft timeline and follow-up action items.

alice (oncall): Final status (14:59:38Z): mitigation applied, routing stabilized, customer impact limited to free-tier latency/failures; enterprise SLAs unaffected. Keeping channel open for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

cara-pm: Adding business impact note: small set of free-tier customers affected; no revenue SLA breaches. We'll include outreach log in postmortem.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: P1 -> mitigated and contained at 2025-11-07T14:59:38Z. Please start RCA thread and include the timeline and artifacts.

alice (oncall): Closing on-call handoff: I'll create the formal postmortem doc and link artifacts. Quick actions before PM: 1) revert or properly gate cfg-2025-11-07-348 2) add canary to fallback weight changes 3) add kv-cache TTL alert. Assigning owners in doc.

ben-sre: I'll open the revert PR and include a unit test for fallback weight sanity checks.

devon-eng: I'll add CI gating for control-plane commits that touch routing weights.

frank-net: I'll add an alert rule: if `kvcache hit=false` spikes > 15% in 5m for region_pref keys, page oncall.

eve-cs: I'll follow up with ACME and send a short summary once postmortem is ready.

alice (oncall): Thanks all — moving this thread to postmortem prep. Leaving channel open for further notes.
